title: Eventual vanishing of a homomorphism zero on an open complement
statement: Let X be a locally Noetherian quasi-compact scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], I a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, F a quasi-coherent module, and G a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent]. Write j_n:I^n G -> G for the image-defined inclusion [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. Let U be an open consisting exactly of points where I_x -> O_X,x is surjective. If chi:I^n G -> F restricts to zero on U [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], then there exist m >= n such that every r:I^m G -> I^n G satisfying r followed by j_n equal to j_m has r followed by chi equal to zero. This asserts only eventual vanishing, not extension or existence of the transition maps.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YB (lemma-homs-over-open), omitted injectivity, expanded with Lemma 01Y9

proof.text: Quasi-coherence of each ideal power follows from the ideal-times-quasi-coherent affine theorem (with exponent zero the quasi-coherent unit). Tensor quasi-coherence and the abelian image/image isomorphism show that H = I^n G is quasi-coherent. Its inclusion in G is mono, so the coherent submodule clause gives coherence of H. Tensor induction and the affine image-section formula compute the range of each power-product inclusion as I(W)^k times G(W), including k = 0.

Let Q be the canonical abelian image of chi. The quasi-coherent cokernel/image theorem gives quasi-coherence of Q and equality of its affine inclusion range with the range of chi. Injectivity of the image inclusion implies that the canonical map H(W) to Q(W) is surjective. H has finite affine sections by the coherent affine-sections theorem. Its quotient Q(W) is finite; the affine-cover finite-type criterion and the coherent/finite-type criterion make Q coherent. If x lies in U, represent each germ of H at x on an open V and restrict to V intersect U; the zero over-site restriction of chi makes its stalk map zero. Stalk exactness gives an epimorphic stalk image factor and a monomorphic stalk image inclusion, so Q_x is zero. Thus the nonzero-stalk locus of Q lies in the nonsurjective-stalk locus of I, by hU.

Apply the support-power-ideal theorem to Q to obtain t with I^t Q zero. The affine-cover detection theorem translates this into I(W)^t contained in the annihilator of Q(W) on every affine W. Set m = n+t. For any r satisfying r followed by j_n equal to j_m, its affine section image under the injective j_n belongs to I(W)^(n+t) G(W) = I(W)^t range(j_n). The linear submodule identity map(I^t top,j_n) = I^t range(j_n) and injectivity imply that r(s) lies in I(W)^t H(W). Induction on sums of scalar multiples, linearity of the canonical image factor, and the annihilation of Q(W) show chi(r(s)) = 0. Sheaf separatedness on the affine basis implies r followed by chi is zero globally. This works for every factor r without choosing a transition map; the argument includes exponent zero and the empty scheme.

lean.statement:
theorem coherent_hom_ideal_power_eventually_zero {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [CompactSpace X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F G : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hG : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace G) (U : X.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ x : X, x ∈ U ↔ Function.Surjective
      ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).map I.toModulesι).hom)
    (n : ℕ) (χ : idealModuleProduct (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).2 G ⟶ F)
    (hχ : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor X.ringCatSheaf U).map χ = 0) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (_ : n ≤ m),
      ∀ r : idealModuleProduct (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).2 G ⟶
          idealModuleProduct (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).2 G,
        r ≫ idealModuleProductι (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).2 G =
          idealModuleProductι (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).2 G → r ≫ χ = 0
